episode_title: StorONE FlashSPAN in action, how 9x capacity increases proved critical with 1PB+ of production data

real_qa.q: How does StoreOne FlashSPAN technology enable 9x capacity increase with mixed flash and HDD storage tiers?
real_qa.r: The 9x ratio combines one part flash with nine parts HDD, achieving hard drive economics with flash performance. The platform allows tuning the SSD layer to the HDD layer based on I/O patterns and application needs. By running an 80-20 rule where 20% of virtual machines consume 80% of infrastructure resources, less critical applications can run on HDD and automatically adjust when needed, with the ability to tune caching on the fly through telemetry.
real_qa.requete: StoreOne FlashSPAN 9x capacity increase how it works

real_qa.q: What one-to-many replication capabilities does StoreOne provide that competitors lack?
real_qa.r: StoreOne's one-to-many replication allows replicating a single primary data source to multiple secondary targets with different snapshot rules per target. Fabrics for Clouds uses this for N+1 disaster recovery across four locations: two in Canada and two in the US, with mixed synchronous local and asynchronous remote replication patterns, and the ability to tier replication across sites while protecting against ransomware.

real_qa.q: How does StoreOne auto-tiering address hardware cost inflation and storage procurement challenges?
real_qa.r: Auto-tiering, a core architectural feature from StoreOne's inception, automatically places data on the appropriate storage medium. With NVMe costs skyrocketing and HDD becoming more economical, customers can add a second petabyte of HDD for less than 100 terabytes of NVMe, averaging storage costs across tiers and extending infrastructure life longer without requiring full flash upgrades.
real_qa.requete: StoreOne auto-tiering HDD SSD cost economics

real_qa.q: Why did Fabrics for Clouds stay with StoreOne for seven years after switching vendors four times in the previous seven years?
real_qa.r: StoreOne's flexible platform architecture separates hardware from software and protocols, allowing it to adopt new technologies immediately. The company's culture of listening to customer requirements, delivering promised features on time, and proactively supporting emerging protocols like NVMe TCP without requiring customer requests proved decisive, combined with the ability to scale through multi-location deployments and auto-tiering without vendor changes.
real_qa.requete: Fabrics for Clouds StoreOne seven years vendor loyalty

real_qa.q: How does AI data generation impact storage strategy and what does StoreOne enable for AI workload management?
real_qa.r: AI workloads generate ten times more data than traditional applications through verbose context and RAG processing. This forces enterprises to adopt staging and de-staging strategies rather than infinite flash purchases. StoreOne's platform enables managing data lifecycle through replication, tiering, and remote boot capabilities, allowing customers to adapt storage economics to massive AI-generated datasets without bankrupting infrastructure budgets.
real_qa.requete: AI workload data storage staging de-staging strategy

guest.bio_context: André Meydoud has been in the infrastructure space for over 30 years. He was involved with virtualized storage concepts in the late 1990s and early 2000s, and has been a long-time advocate of software-defined storage since around 2010. He began working with StoreOne approximately seven years ago after a four-hour conversation with StoreOne co-founder Galza Nau, and has deployed StoreOne across multiple data centers in Canada and the US managing approximately 1.2 petabytes of production data.
